title: Measurement of Force-Sensitive Protein Dynamics in Living Cells Using a Combination of Fluorescent Techniques
protocol: Clone tension sensor construct into pRRL vector or other viral expression plasmid.
Generate lentivirus in Human Embryonic Kidney (HEK) 293T cells using psPax2 and pMD2.G packaging plasmids.
Transduce desired cells with virus using standard transduction protocols.
Sort cells using flow cytometry, selecting a homogeneous population expressing each construct at approximately endogenous levels.
Conduct experiments immediately after sorting or cryogenically freeze cells for later use.
Do not exceed 2 freeze-thaw cycles for a given stable cell line.
Use cell lines deficient in the protein of interest to increase signal-to-noise ratio and limit over-expression artifacts.
Prepare substrates for cell seeding.
Acquire 4, 35 mm glass-bottomed dishes.
In a cell culture hood, make 4 mL of 10 µg/mL fibronectin solution in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) using sterile PBS.
Gently invert the tube once to mix.
Let the solution sit for 5 min in the cell culture hood.
Pipette 1 mL of fibronectin solution onto each glass-bottomed dish.
Incubate the dishes with fibronectin for 1 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C.
Aspirate the fibronectin solution from the dishes.
Rinse once with PBS and add 1 mL of PBS to each dish.
Seed cells onto prepared substrates.
Rinse the cells once with 3 mL of PBS.
Add 1 mL of 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA and incubate for 5 min at 37 °C.
Add 3 mL of complete media to the 6 cm dish, collect the cells, and place into a 15 mL conical tube.
Spin the cells down at 1000 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the media and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of complete media.
Remove PBS from fibronectin-coated glass dishes.
Count the cells and seed 30,000 cells onto each fibronectin-coated glass dish with appropriate complete media for a final volume of 1.5 mL.
Allow the cells to spread for 4 h following seeding.
Aspirate growth media at 2 h of spreading.
Rinse once with imaging media, leaving 1.5 ml of imaging media.
Turn on the microscope.
Turn on the arc lamp first.
Turn on the filter wheel controller.
Turn on the automated stage controller.
Turn on the microscope-computer interface.
Turn on the camera.
Turn on the FRAP laser.
Turn on the laser position controllers.
Turn on the computer and open microscope control software.
Allow 15 min for the arc lamp to warm up.
Allow 15 min for the FRAP laser to warm up.
Calibrate the FRAP laser.
Open the laser configuration window.
Set Illumination Setting (during pulse) to appropriate settings for laser exposure to the sample.
Set Illumination Setting (during imaging) to illumination settings appropriate for imaging only the acceptor fluorophore.
Select the objective to calibrate under Coordinate System Setting.
Uncheck Manually Click Calibration Points.
Check Display images during calibration.
Set Dwell time to 10,000 µs and number of pulses to 100.
Place the calibration slide into the stage adaptor with the coverslip side down.
Fix cells expressing the tension sensor with 4% paraformaldehyde for 10 min.
Place fixed samples in PBS after fixation.
Rinse the sample three times with PBS and leave in PBS.
Place the sample into the microscope stage holder for imaging.
Open the Multi-Dimensional Acquisition (MDA) tool.
Establish sequential imaging of three channels: acceptor only excitation and emission, donor excitation and acceptor emission, and donor only excitation and emission.
Scan the sample using an exposure time of 500 ms and a neutral density filter of 10%.
Find a cell expressing the tension sensor with clear localization to a structure of interest.
Select an exposure time of 500 ms for each imaging channel.
Acquire a FRET image sequence using an ND filter of 100%.
Estimate the average intensity of the sensor at subcellular structures of interest in each imaging channel.
Ensure intensities are above 6,000 for a 16-bit camera to avoid inaccurate results due to improper correction estimates or background signals.
Use identical optical settings (exposure times, filters, objectives) for all FRET experiments being compared.
Acquire a second FRET image sequence of the same field of view.
Estimate photobleaching between frames by comparing average intensity of the sensor in each imaging channel.
Adjust the imaging parameters to maximize the intensity while minimizing photobleaching.
For coarse adjustments, change the ND filter being used during acquisition.
For finer adjustments, change the exposure time in steps of 250 ms.
Repeat Steps 3.5 – 3.8 until adequate signal can be obtained while minimizing photobleaching.
Optimize the laser settings to ensure complete bleaching of the region of interest (ROI) without bleaching the surrounding area or causing photodamage.
Fix one of the generated samples of the cells expressing the tension sensor with 4% paraformaldehyde for 10 min.
Rinse the sample three times with PBS and leave in PBS.
Place the sample into the microscope stage holder for imaging.
Open the laser configuration window.
Set a laser dwell time of 1,000 µs and 10 pulses.
Find a cell expressing the tension sensor with clear localization to a structure of interest.
Acquire an image.
Draw a rectangular ROI outlining the area to bleach.
Store the ROI location.
Pulse the laser.
Snap another image of the sample.
Check that the entire ROI is bleached such that the intensity is near background levels.
Make sure there is no bleaching outside of the ROI.
Adjust the laser settings as needed to achieve significant bleaching within the ROI without inducing significant bleaching outside the ROI.
Raise and lower the dwell time in steps of 100 µs for coarse adjustments.
Raise and lower the number of pulses in steps of 5 pulses for fine adjustments.
Repeat Steps 4.1.5 – 4.1.8 until reaching the minimum settings at which the ROI is fully bleached without off-target photobleaching.
Prepare the microscopy set-up for live cell imaging, preferably with a heated stage and objective as well as CO2 control.
Allow the set-up to equilibrate for 20 min.
Place one of the generated samples of cells expressing the tension sensor into the microscope stage holder for imaging.
Allow the sample to equilibrate for 10 min.
Using the MDA tool, set up a time-lapse to acquire 3-5 images pre-bleach.
Bleach the region of interest (ROI).
Continue taking 10-60 images post-bleach.
Image vinculin at focal adhesions every 5 seconds for 5 minutes to observe dynamics without excessive bleaching.
Use acceptor imaging settings that minimize exposure to light while maintaining a sufficient signal-to-noise ratio.
Snap an image of a cell expressing the tension sensor with clear localization to a structure of interest.
Draw a rectangular ROI to highlight where to bleach and store the ROI location.
Initiate the time-lapse.
Examine resulting images for potential issues such as substantial jumps in fluorescence recovery between frames.
Reduce the time-step between frames if there are substantial jumps (greater than 10% of initial intensity).

Reduce the number of images taken post-bleach or change imaging settings to reduce exposure of the sample to light if there is a significant global loss of fluorescence over time (greater than 5-10% of initial intensity).
Increase the total length of the time-lapse if fluorescence recovery has not plateaued by the end.
Adjust time-lapse parameters accordingly.
Repeat Steps 4.2.5 – 4.2.7 until fluorescence recovery is adequately captured without global photo-damage to the sample.
Prepare the microscopy set-up for live cell imaging with a heated stage and objective, CO2 control if available.
Allow the set-up to equilibrate for 20 minutes.
Maintain the temperature at 37 °C in the imaging chamber.
Use a peristaltic pump to pass humidified 5% CO2 over the sample at 15 mL/min to maintain pH.
Alternatively, use live imaging media containing HEPES if CO2 control is unavailable.
Open the MDA tool and set up with FRET imaging parameters including different filter sets.
Save this MDA to the experimental folder as MDA_FRET_Date.
Set up another MDA with FRAP imaging parameters including different filter sets, time-lapse settings, and journal to pulse the laser after pre-bleach acquisition.
Save this MDA to the experimental folder as MDA_FRAP_Date.
Close the MDA window.
Select Journal | Start Recording from the toolbar at the top of the screen.
Open the MDA window, load the MDA_FRET_Date state, and press Acquire.
Load the MDA_FRAP_Date state and press Acquire.
At the end of acquisition, select Journal | Stop Recording from the toolbar.
Save this journal to the experimental folder with the name FRETFRAP_Date and add it to a toolbar for easy access.
Close the MDA window.
Place one of the generated samples of cells expressing the tension sensor into the microscope holder for imaging.
Allow the sample to equilibrate for 10 minutes.
Navigate the sample using image acquisition under Acquire | Acquire with minimal exposure time and ND filter to identify the cells of interest.
Set continuous autofocus by navigating to Devices | Focus.
Manually focus on the sample until reaching the correct imaging plane.
Click Set Continuous Focus, wait for the system to adjust, and click Start Continuous Focusing.
Find a cell expressing the tension sensor with clear localization to a structure of interest and snap an image.
Draw a rectangular ROI to highlight where to bleach.
Store the ROI location.
Initialize the FRETFRAP_Date journal, which will begin the acquisition of FRET images followed by the initialization of the FRAP time-lapse.
Repeat steps until 10-15 image sets are acquired.
Analyze the FRET images using the software of choice.
Quantify relevant parameters for each subcellular structure that was bleached.
Analyze the FRAP images using the software of choice.
Correct recovery data for bleaching effects.
Normalize corrected data to pre-bleach intensities.
Quantify the half-time of recovery using the equation τ1/2 = ln 2/k.
Calculate the mobile fraction according to MF - (MF - Ro)e-kt.
Interpret FRET-FRAP data.
Compile relevant information for each ROI including: FRET index/efficiency, acceptor intensity, FRAP half-time, FRAP mobile fraction.
